name: net_gap_repair
description: Client 1 hangs while 1,220 turns pile up on its link, and the link loses 1,200 of them, as a full browser buffer does. TURN_REQUEST repairs the gap a window of 100 turns at a time; the client waits half of turn_request_ms and a turn between requests, so the sequencer (which answers a seat at most once per half of turn_request_ms, as the server does) ignores none of them, and the gap closes in about 3.6 s, not 6.7 s (review M1 protocol 2). Afterwards both clients hash alike.

steps.msg: 1,200 turns were lost on the way
the hung client reads on and sees its gap of 1,200 turns
the gap was repaired and the client plays on
a window an answer, and no request came too soon to be answered
1,200 turns in at most 4 s (twelve windows, one each 300 ms)
and both clients hash alike afterwards
